prerequisites: The course should be taken before “Hybrid control systems and Digital Signal Processing” and “Dynamic control of AC machines”.

learning_outcomes.text: To analyze and model electromechanical systems, from the point of view of the mechanical and electrical systems.
To design control systems for electrical drives, with the implementation of the most used control loops in these systems.
To analyze different examples of electromechanical systems, their use in power systems and the particular constraints for the control systems.
To know the most common actuators used in electromechanical systems, as well as their limitations from a point of view of dynamic control.

syllabus_topics: Module I. Analysis and dynamic modelling of electromechanical systems:
T1: Dynamic modelling of physical systems.
T2: Dynamic modelling of electromechanical systems.
T3: Dynamic analysis of electromechanical systems.
Module II. Principles of control of electromechanical systems:
T5: Design specifications and basic control actions.
Module III. Design, topologies and control limits on electromechanical systems:
teaching_methods: Computer aid tools for problem resolution
Final assignment with an open design problem

assessment_methods.method: Written exam at the end of classes
Assignment to be presented before the final exam (documentation)
Assignment to be presented before the final exam (presentation)

assessment_rules: A minimum score of 4/10 is needed for the written exam to pass the subject. A minimum score of 4/10 is needed for the assignment to pass the subject. The assignment consists of an 8-page report and a 15-minute presentation. Practical cases involve solving three problems using Matlab.
bibliography: "Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems”, Gene F. Franklin, J. David Powell, Abbas Emani-Naeini. 5th Edition, Prentice Hall.
